title: Two routing seams still judge without the lane-routing predicate: core's sequential termination check and the triage registry factory
summary: Deferred from the architect's review of fix/routing-honors-sandbox-deny (2026-09-26, APPROVE-WITH-MINOR). (m2) core/triage_termination.go:116 hasClaimableInboxWork calls inboxbatch.PartitionConsole(items, nil). When a lane-forbidden item (protected or builder-sandbox-denied) is the only pending work, triage correctly commits nothing, but this check calls the item claimable, and cycle_closeout.go:44-48 then seals the sequential cycle FAIL. (m4) The triage phase-registry factory (triage.go init, used by serve-phase and `evolve phase triage`) builds triage.Config with no LaneForbidden. Those paths silently fall back to protected surface only, which contradicts the 'degrades loudly' contract. (m9) The [routing] WARN from laneForbidden goes only to stderr; the coordinator has a Signal Center that could carry it as a coded event.
fix: Inject the lane predicate into core with an orchestrator option (core cannot import the composition root), and use it in hasClaimableInboxWork. Give the registry factory the same predicate, built from req.ProjectRoot through lanerouting.Forbidden with the build profile name, with a loud fallback. Register a Signal Center code for the routing-fallback warning.
acceptance: A sequential cycle whose only pending item is lane-forbidden does not seal FAIL on the termination check (test)
serve-phase and evolve phase triage judge with the lane predicate (test)
The routing fallback emits a registered coded signal
(from triage-termination-scope-aware) RED first: a sequential cycle whose root holds only an item declaring a protected file ends as planned no-work, not claim-failed
(from triage-termination-scope-aware) Every production composition root wires the predicate (root-coverage pin); a nil predicate is allowed only on the pinned test root
(from triage-termination-scope-aware) The lane path is unchanged (triage_termination_lane_test.go stays green)

(merged at the inbox review 2026-09-27) Absorbs triage-termination-scope-aware's acceptance (RED-first sequential protected-only root ends as planned no-work; a root-coverage pin with nil only on routingtest; the lane path unchanged) and its F30 addendum evidence. Add: dispatchableIDs must use the W3 rule (inboxmover.ResolveDispatchability or PendingDispatchability plus the lane predicate). As it stands it is a sixth copy of the 'may a lane take this id' belief W3 unified. Land it with or before the W3 merge.
